WITH federal_rebate_timeline AS (
    -- First CTE: Build federal rebate timeline
    SELECT
        fi.federal_incentive_id,
        fi.incentive_name,
        fi.incentive_type,
        fi.effective_date,
        fi.expiration_date,
        fi.incentive_amount_usd,
        fi.incentive_percentage,
        fi.maximum_incentive_usd,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (fi.expiration_date - fi.effective_date)) / 86400 AS days_active,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (fi.expiration_date - CURRENT_DATE)) / 86400 AS days_until_expiration,
        CASE
            WHEN fi.expiration_date IS NULL THEN 'No Expiration'
            WHEN fi.expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE THEN 'Active'
            ELSE 'Expired'
        END AS status
    FROM federal_incentives fi
    WHERE 'Solar Photovoltaics' = ANY(fi.eligible_technologies)
),
state_rebate_timeline AS (
    -- Second CTE: Build state rebate timeline
    SELECT
        si.state_incentive_id,
        si.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        si.incentive_name,
        si.incentive_type,
        si.effective_date,
        si.expiration_date,
        si.incentive_amount_usd,
        si.incentive_percentage,
        si.maximum_incentive_usd,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (si.expiration_date - si.effective_date)) / 86400 AS days_active,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (si.expiration_date - CURRENT_DATE)) / 86400 AS days_until_expiration,
        CASE
            WHEN si.expiration_date IS NULL THEN 'No Expiration'
            WHEN si.expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE THEN 'Active'
            ELSE 'Expired'
        END AS status
    FROM state_incentives si
    INNER JOIN states s ON si.state_id = s.state_id
    WHERE 'Solar Photovoltaics' = ANY(si.eligible_technologies)
),
utility_rebate_timeline AS (
    -- Third CTE: Build utility rebate timeline
    SELECT
        ui.utility_incentive_id,
        ui.utility_id,
        uc.utility_name,
        ui.state_id,
        ui.incentive_name,
        ui.incentive_type,
        ui.effective_date,
        ui.expiration_date,
        ui.incentive_amount_usd,
        ui.incentive_percentage,
        ui.maximum_incentive_usd,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ui.expiration_date - ui.effective_date)) / 86400 AS days_active,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (ui.expiration_date - CURRENT_DATE)) / 86400 AS days_until_expiration,
        CASE
            WHEN ui.expiration_date IS NULL THEN 'No Expiration'
            WHEN ui.expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE THEN 'Active'
            ELSE 'Expired'
        END AS status
    FROM utility_incentives ui
    INNER JOIN utility_companies uc ON ui.utility_id = uc.utility_id
    WHERE 'Solar Photovoltaics' = ANY(ui.eligible_technologies)
),
rebate_expiration_analysis AS (
    -- Fourth CTE: Analyze rebate expirations
    SELECT
        'Federal' AS rebate_level,
        COUNT(*) AS total_rebates,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Active' THEN 1 END) AS active_rebates,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Expired' THEN 1 END) AS expired_rebates,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 0 AND 90 THEN 1 END) AS expiring_90days,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 91 AND 180 THEN 1 END) AS expiring_180days,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 181 AND 365 THEN 1 END) AS expiring_1year,
        AVG(days_until_expiration) AS avg_days_until_expiration,
        MIN(days_until_expiration) AS min_days_until_expiration
    FROM federal_rebate_timeline
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        'State' AS rebate_level,
        COUNT(*),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Active' THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Expired' THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 0 AND 90 THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 91 AND 180 THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 181 AND 365 THEN 1 END),
        AVG(days_until_expiration),
        MIN(days_until_expiration)
    FROM state_rebate_timeline
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        'Utility' AS rebate_level,
        COUNT(*),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Active' THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN status = 'Expired' THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 0 AND 90 THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 91 AND 180 THEN 1 END),
        COUNT(CASE WHEN days_until_expiration BETWEEN 181 AND 365 THEN 1 END),
        AVG(days_until_expiration),
        MIN(days_until_expiration)
    FROM utility_rebate_timeline
),
rebate_trend_analysis AS (
    -- Fifth CTE: Analyze rebate trends over time
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('year', effective_date) AS year,
        DATE_TRUNC('quarter', effective_date) AS quarter,
        COUNT(*) AS rebates_introduced,
        AVG(incentive_amount_usd) AS avg_incentive_amount,
        SUM(incentive_amount_usd) AS total_incentive_value
    FROM (
        SELECT effective_date, incentive_amount_usd FROM federal_rebate_timeline
        UNION ALL
        SELECT effective_date, incentive_amount_usd FROM state_rebate_timeline
        UNION ALL
        SELECT effective_date, incentive_amount_usd FROM utility_rebate_timeline
    ) all_rebates
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('year', effective_date), DATE_TRUNC('quarter', effective_date)
),
final_expiration_intelligence AS (
    -- Sixth CTE: Final expiration intelligence
    SELECT
        rea.*,
        ROUND(CAST(rea.avg_days_until_expiration AS NUMERIC), 0) AS avg_days_until_expiration,
        ROUND(CAST(rea.min_days_until_expiration AS NUMERIC), 0) AS min_days_until_expiration,
        CASE
            WHEN rea.expiring_90days > 0 THEN 'High Expiration Risk'
            WHEN rea.expiring_180days > 0 THEN 'Moderate Expiration Risk'
            WHEN rea.expiring_1year > 0 THEN 'Low Expiration Risk'
            ELSE 'No Near-Term Expirations'
        END AS expiration_risk_level
    FROM rebate_expiration_analysis rea
)
SELECT
    rebate_level, total_rebates, active_rebates, expired_rebates,
    expiring_90days, expiring_180days, expiring_1year,
    avg_days_until_expiration, min_days_until_expiration, expiration_risk_level
FROM final_expiration_intelligence
ORDER BY rebate_level;

Query 12: Geographic Rate Optimization with Zip Code Level Analysis {#query-12}

Use Case: Location-Based Rate Optimization Platform - Zip Code Level Rate Analysis for Energy Consultants

Description: Enterprise-level geographic rate optimization with zip code level intelligence, location-based rate recommendations, and comprehensive geographic cost analysis. Demonstrates production patterns used by location-based rate optimization platforms and geographic intelligence systems.

Use Case: Location-Based Rate Optimization Platform - Zip Code Level Rate Analysis for Energy Consultants

Business Value: Comprehensive geographic rate optimization showing optimal rates by zip code, location-based recommendations, and geographic cost analysis. Enables energy consultants to provide location-specific rate recommendations.

Purpose: Optimizes rates by geographic location enabling consultants to provide location-specific recommendations and cost analysis.

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), geographic aggregations, zip code analysis, location-based optimization, spatial matching, complex joins

Expected Output: Geographic rate optimization with zip code level intelligence and location-based recommendations.

WITH zip_code_rate_analysis AS (
    -- First CTE: Analyze rates by zip code
    SELECT
        zc.zip_code,
        zc.city,
        zc.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        zc.county_id,
        c.county_name,
        zc.latitude,
        zc.longitude,
        COUNT(DISTINCT gra.rate_structure_id) AS available_rate_structures,
        COUNT(DISTINCT gra.utility_id) AS utilities_serving_zip,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS avg_zip_rate,
        MIN(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS min_zip_rate,
        MAX(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS max_zip_rate,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS median_zip_rate
    FROM zip_codes zc
    INNER JOIN states s ON zc.state_id = s.state_id
    LEFT JOIN counties c ON zc.county_id = c.county_id
    LEFT JOIN geographic_rate_areas gra ON zc.zip_code = gra.zip_code
    LEFT JOIN electricity_rates er ON gra.rate_structure_id = er.rate_structure_id
    WHERE er.is_current = TRUE
    GROUP BY zc.zip_code, zc.city, zc.state_id, s.state_name, zc.county_id, c.county_name, zc.latitude, zc.longitude
),
county_rate_benchmarks AS (
    -- Second CTE: Calculate county-level benchmarks
    SELECT
        c.county_id,
        c.county_name,
        c.state_id,
        AVG(zcra.avg_zip_rate) AS county_avg_rate,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY zcra.avg_zip_rate) AS county_median_rate,
        MIN(zcra.avg_zip_rate) AS county_min_rate,
        MAX(zcra.avg_zip_rate) AS county_max_rate
    FROM zip_code_rate_analysis zcra
    INNER JOIN counties c ON zcra.county_id = c.county_id
    GROUP BY c.county_id, c.county_name, c.state_id
),
state_rate_benchmarks AS (
    -- Third CTE: Calculate state-level benchmarks
    SELECT
        s.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        AVG(zcra.avg_zip_rate) AS state_avg_rate,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY zcra.avg_zip_rate) AS state_median_rate
    FROM zip_code_rate_analysis zcra
    INNER JOIN states s ON zcra.state_id = s.state_id
    GROUP BY s.state_id, s.state_name
),
zip_code_optimization AS (
    -- Fourth CTE: Optimize rates by zip code
    SELECT
        zcra.*,
        crb.county_avg_rate,
        crb.county_median_rate,
        crb.county_min_rate,
        crb.county_max_rate,
        srb.state_avg_rate,
        srb.state_median_rate,
        -- Optimization metrics
        zcra.avg_zip_rate - crb.county_avg_rate AS difference_from_county_avg,
        CASE
            WHEN crb.county_avg_rate > 0 THEN
                ((zcra.avg_zip_rate - crb.county_avg_rate) / crb.county_avg_rate) * 100
            ELSE NULL
        END AS difference_from_county_avg_percentage,
        zcra.avg_zip_rate - srb.state_avg_rate AS difference_from_state_avg,
        CASE
            WHEN srb.state_avg_rate > 0 THEN
                ((zcra.avg_zip_rate - srb.state_avg_rate) / srb.state_avg_rate) * 100
            ELSE NULL
        END AS difference_from_state_avg_percentage,
        -- Rate competitiveness
        CASE
            WHEN zcra.avg_zip_rate <= crb.county_min_rate THEN 'Most Competitive'
            WHEN zcra.avg_zip_rate <= crb.county_median_rate THEN 'Competitive'
            WHEN zcra.avg_zip_rate <= crb.county_avg_rate THEN 'Average'
            ELSE 'Above Average'
        END AS competitiveness_classification
    FROM zip_code_rate_analysis zcra
    LEFT JOIN county_rate_benchmarks crb ON zcra.county_id = crb.county_id
    INNER JOIN state_rate_benchmarks srb ON zcra.state_id = srb.state_id
),
final_geographic_optimization AS (
    -- Fifth CTE: Final geographic optimization
    SELECT
        zco.*,
        ROUND(CAST(zco.difference_from_county_avg AS NUMERIC), 6) AS difference_from_county_avg,
        ROUND(CAST(zco.difference_from_county_avg_percentage AS NUMERIC), 2) AS difference_from_county_avg_percentage,
        ROUND(CAST(zco.difference_from_state_avg AS NUMERIC), 6) AS difference_from_state_avg,
        ROUND(CAST(zco.difference_from_state_avg_percentage AS NUMERIC), 2) AS difference_from_state_avg_percentage,
        -- Window functions for ranking
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY zco.state_id ORDER BY zco.avg_zip_rate) AS state_rate_rank,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY zco.state_id ORDER BY zco.avg_zip_rate) AS state_rate_percentile
    FROM zip_code_optimization zco
)
SELECT
    zip_code, city, state_id, state_name, county_id, county_name,
    latitude, longitude, available_rate_structures, utilities_serving_zip,
    ROUND(CAST(avg_zip_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS avg_zip_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(min_zip_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS min_zip_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(max_zip_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS max_zip_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(median_zip_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS median_zip_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(county_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS county_avg_rate,
    difference_from_county_avg, difference_from_county_avg_percentage,
    ROUND(CAST(state_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS state_avg_rate,
    difference_from_state_avg, difference_from_state_avg_percentage,
    competitiveness_classification, state_rate_rank,
    ROUND(CAST(state_rate_percentile * 100 AS NUMERIC), 2) AS state_rate_percentile
FROM final_geographic_optimization
ORDER BY state_name, avg_zip_rate;

Query 13: Utility Rate Portfolio Analysis with Rate Code Diversity Metrics {#query-13}

Use Case: Utility Portfolio Management Platform - Rate Code Diversity Analysis for Utility Strategists

Description: Enterprise-level utility rate portfolio analysis with rate code diversity metrics, portfolio optimization, and comprehensive rate offering analysis. Demonstrates production patterns used by utility portfolio management platforms and rate strategy systems.

Use Case: Utility Portfolio Management Platform - Rate Code Diversity Analysis for Utility Strategists

Business Value: Comprehensive utility rate portfolio analysis showing rate code diversity, portfolio optimization opportunities, and comprehensive rate offering metrics. Enables utility strategists to optimize rate portfolios and identify gaps.

Purpose: Analyzes utility rate portfolios enabling strategists to understand portfolio diversity, identify optimization opportunities, and optimize rate offerings.

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), portfolio analysis, diversity metrics, optimization calculations, rate offering analysis, window functions

Expected Output: Utility rate portfolio analysis with diversity metrics and optimization recommendations.

WITH utility_rate_portfolio AS (
    -- First CTE: Build utility rate portfolio
    SELECT
        uc.utility_id,
        uc.utility_name,
        uc.utility_type,
        uc.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_code_id) AS rate_codes_offered,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_id) AS total_rates,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_type) AS rate_types_offered,
        COUNT(DISTINCT rc.rate_structure_type) AS structure_types_offered,
        COUNT(DISTINCT rc.sector) AS sectors_covered,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS portfolio_avg_rate,
        MIN(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS portfolio_min_rate,
        MAX(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS portfolio_max_rate,
        STDDEV(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS portfolio_rate_stddev
    FROM utility_companies uc
    INNER JOIN states s ON uc.state_id = s.state_id
    INNER JOIN electricity_rates er ON uc.utility_id = er.utility_id
    INNER JOIN rate_codes rc ON er.rate_code_id = rc.rate_code_id
    WHERE er.is_current = TRUE AND uc.is_active = TRUE
    GROUP BY uc.utility_id, uc.utility_name, uc.utility_type, uc.state_id, s.state_name
),
state_portfolio_benchmarks AS (
    -- Second CTE: Calculate state portfolio benchmarks
    SELECT
        urp.state_id,
        AVG(urp.rate_codes_offered) AS state_avg_rate_codes,
        AVG(urp.total_rates) AS state_avg_total_rates,
        AVG(urp.rate_types_offered) AS state_avg_rate_types,
        AVG(urp.structure_types_offered) AS state_avg_structure_types,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY urp.rate_codes_offered) AS state_median_rate_codes
    FROM utility_rate_portfolio urp
    GROUP BY urp.state_id
),
portfolio_diversity_metrics AS (
    -- Third CTE: Calculate portfolio diversity metrics
    SELECT
        urp.*,
        spb.state_avg_rate_codes,
        spb.state_avg_total_rates,
        spb.state_avg_rate_types,
        spb.state_avg_structure_types,
        spb.state_median_rate_codes,
        -- Diversity score (weighted)
        (urp.rate_codes_offered * 2.0) +
        (urp.rate_types_offered * 1.5) +
        (urp.structure_types_offered * 1.0) +
        (urp.sectors_covered * 1.5) AS diversity_score,
        -- Portfolio completeness
        CASE
            WHEN urp.rate_types_offered >= 3 AND urp.sectors_covered >= 3 THEN 'Complete Portfolio'
            WHEN urp.rate_types_offered >= 2 AND urp.sectors_covered >= 2 THEN 'Moderate Portfolio'
            ELSE 'Limited Portfolio'
        END AS portfolio_completeness,
        -- Rate range diversity
        CASE
            WHEN urp.portfolio_max_rate - urp.portfolio_min_rate > urp.portfolio_avg_rate * 0.3 THEN 'High Diversity'
            WHEN urp.portfolio_max_rate - urp.portfolio_min_rate > urp.portfolio_avg_rate * 0.15 THEN 'Moderate Diversity'
            ELSE 'Low Diversity'
        END AS rate_range_diversity
    FROM utility_rate_portfolio urp
    INNER JOIN state_portfolio_benchmarks spb ON urp.state_id = spb.state_id
),
final_portfolio_analysis AS (
    -- Fourth CTE: Final portfolio analysis
    SELECT
        pdm.*,
        ROUND(CAST(pdm.diversity_score AS NUMERIC), 2) AS diversity_score,
        -- Portfolio positioning
        CASE
            WHEN pdm.rate_codes_offered > pdm.state_avg_rate_codes THEN 'Above State Average'
            WHEN pdm.rate_codes_offered = pdm.state_avg_rate_codes THEN 'At State Average'
            ELSE 'Below State Average'
        END AS portfolio_positioning,
        -- Optimization recommendations
        CASE
            WHEN pdm.rate_types_offered < 3 THEN 'Consider Adding More Rate Types'
            WHEN pdm.sectors_covered < 3 THEN 'Consider Expanding Sector Coverage'
            WHEN pdm.structure_types_offered < 2 THEN 'Consider Adding Structure Types'
            ELSE 'Portfolio Well Diversified'
        END AS optimization_recommendation
    FROM portfolio_diversity_metrics pdm
)
SELECT
    utility_id, utility_name, utility_type, state_id, state_name,
    rate_codes_offered, total_rates, rate_types_offered, structure_types_offered, sectors_covered,
    ROUND(CAST(portfolio_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS portfolio_avg_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(portfolio_min_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS portfolio_min_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(portfolio_max_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS portfolio_max_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(state_avg_rate_codes AS NUMERIC), 2) AS state_avg_rate_codes,
    diversity_score, portfolio_completeness, rate_range_diversity,
    portfolio_positioning, optimization_recommendation
FROM final_portfolio_analysis
ORDER BY state_name, diversity_score DESC;

Query 14: Solar Installation Economics with Net Metering Analysis {#query-14}

Use Case: Solar Economics Platform - Installation Economics and Net Metering Analysis for Solar Installers

Description: Enterprise-level solar installation economics analysis with net metering analysis, feed-in tariff evaluation, and comprehensive financial modeling. Demonstrates production patterns used by solar economics platforms and installation financial analysis systems.

Use Case: Solar Economics Platform - Installation Economics and Net Metering Analysis for Solar Installers

Business Value: Comprehensive solar installation economics showing net metering benefits, feed-in tariff analysis, and financial modeling. Enables solar installers to provide accurate economic analysis and installation recommendations.

Purpose: Analyzes solar installation economics enabling installers to provide accurate financial analysis and optimize installation economics.

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (8+ levels), net metering calculations, feed-in tariff analysis, financial modeling, ROI calculations, time-series analysis

Expected Output: Solar installation economics with net metering analysis and financial modeling.

WITH solar_system_economics AS (
    -- First CTE: Define solar system economics
    SELECT
        system_size_kw,
        system_cost_per_watt,
        annual_production_kwh,
        system_cost_per_watt * system_size_kw * 1000 AS total_system_cost
    FROM (VALUES
        (5.0, 3.0, 7500),
        (10.0, 3.0, 15000),
        (20.0, 2.8, 30000),
        (50.0, 2.5, 75000),
        (100.0, 2.3, 150000)
    ) AS systems(system_size_kw, system_cost_per_watt, annual_production_kwh)
),
net_metering_analysis AS (
    -- Second CTE: Analyze net metering programs
    SELECT
        ui.utility_incentive_id,
        ui.utility_id,
        uc.utility_name,
        ui.state_id,
        ui.incentive_type,
        ui.net_metering_capacity_limit_kw,
        ui.feed_in_tariff_rate_usd_per_kwh,
        er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh AS retail_rate,
        CASE
            WHEN ui.feed_in_tariff_rate_usd_per_kwh IS NOT NULL THEN ui.feed_in_tariff_rate_usd_per_kwh
            ELSE er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh
        END AS effective_export_rate
    FROM utility_incentives ui
    INNER JOIN utility_companies uc ON ui.utility_id = uc.utility_id
    LEFT JOIN electricity_rates er ON ui.utility_id = er.utility_id AND er.rate_type = 'Residential'
    WHERE ui.incentive_type IN ('Net Metering', 'Feed-in Tariff')
        AND ui.is_active = TRUE
        AND er.is_current = TRUE
),
solar_economics_calculations AS (
    -- Third CTE: Calculate solar economics
    SELECT
        sse.system_size_kw,
        sse.total_system_cost,
        sse.annual_production_kwh,
        nma.utility_id,
        nma.utility_name,
        nma.state_id,
        nma.retail_rate,
        nma.effective_export_rate,
        nma.net_metering_capacity_limit_kw,
        -- Annual savings (self-consumption + export)
        CASE
            WHEN sse.system_size_kw <= COALESCE(nma.net_metering_capacity_limit_kw, 999999) THEN
                (sse.annual_production_kwh * 0.7 * nma.retail_rate) +  -- Self-consumed
                (sse.annual_production_kwh * 0.3 * nma.effective_export_rate)  -- Exported
            ELSE
                sse.annual_production_kwh * 0.7 * nma.retail_rate  -- Limited by capacity
        END AS annual_savings,
        -- Payback period
        CASE
            WHEN (sse.annual_production_kwh * 0.7 * nma.retail_rate) > 0 THEN
                sse.total_system_cost / (sse.annual_production_kwh * 0.7 * nma.retail_rate)
            ELSE NULL
        END AS payback_period_years
    FROM solar_system_economics sse
    CROSS JOIN net_metering_analysis nma
),
rebate_adjusted_economics AS (
    -- Fourth CTE: Adjust for rebates
    SELECT
        sec.*,
        COALESCE(sra.total_combined_incentives_usd, 0) AS total_rebates,
        sec.total_system_cost - COALESCE(sra.total_combined_incentives_usd, 0) AS net_system_cost,
        CASE
            WHEN sec.annual_savings > 0 THEN
                (sec.total_system_cost - COALESCE(sra.total_combined_incentives_usd, 0)) / sec.annual_savings
            ELSE NULL
        END AS rebate_adjusted_payback_years
    FROM solar_economics_calculations sec
    LEFT JOIN solar_rebate_aggregations sra ON sec.state_id = sra.state_id AND sec.utility_id = sra.utility_id
),
final_economics_analysis AS (
    -- Fifth CTE: Final economics analysis
    SELECT
        rae.*,
        ROUND(CAST(rae.annual_savings AS NUMERIC), 2) AS annual_savings,
        ROUND(CAST(rae.payback_period_years AS NUMERIC), 2) AS payback_period_years,
        ROUND(CAST(rae.total_rebates AS NUMERIC), 2) AS total_rebates,
        ROUND(CAST(rae.net_system_cost AS NUMERIC), 2) AS net_system_cost,
        ROUND(CAST(rae.rebate_adjusted_payback_years AS NUMERIC), 2) AS rebate_adjusted_payback_years,
        -- Investment classification
        CASE
            WHEN rae.rebate_adjusted_payback_years <= 5 THEN 'Excellent Investment'
            WHEN rae.rebate_adjusted_payback_years <= 8 THEN 'Good Investment'
            WHEN rae.rebate_adjusted_payback_years <= 12 THEN 'Moderate Investment'
            ELSE 'Long-Term Investment'
        END AS investment_classification
    FROM rebate_adjusted_economics rae
)
SELECT
    system_size_kw, utility_id, utility_name, state_id,
    ROUND(CAST(total_system_cost AS NUMERIC), 2) AS total_system_cost,
    annual_production_kwh, retail_rate, effective_export_rate,
    annual_savings, payback_period_years, total_rebates, net_system_cost,
    rebate_adjusted_payback_years, investment_classification
FROM final_economics_analysis
ORDER BY state_id, rebate_adjusted_payback_years;

Query 15: Rate Volatility Analysis with Risk Assessment Metrics {#query-15}

Use Case: Rate Risk Analysis Platform - Volatility and Risk Assessment for Energy Risk Managers

Description: Enterprise-level rate volatility analysis with risk assessment metrics, volatility calculations, and comprehensive risk classification. Demonstrates production patterns used by rate risk analysis platforms and volatility assessment systems.

Use Case: Rate Risk Analysis Platform - Volatility and Risk Assessment for Energy Risk Managers

Business Value: Comprehensive rate volatility analysis showing volatility metrics, risk assessments, and risk classifications. Enables energy risk managers to understand rate volatility and manage risk exposure.

Purpose: Analyzes rate volatility enabling risk managers to understand volatility patterns, assess risk levels, and manage risk exposure.

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), volatility calculations, risk metrics, time-series analysis, statistical analysis, window functions

Expected Output: Rate volatility analysis with risk assessment metrics and risk classifications.

WITH historical_rate_volatility AS (
    -- First CTE: Calculate historical rate volatility
    SELECT
        her.utility_id,
        her.rate_code_id,
        her.state_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', her.effective_date) AS rate_month,
        AVG(her.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS monthly_avg_rate,
        STDDEV(her.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS monthly_stddev_rate,
        MIN(her.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS monthly_min_rate,
        MAX(her.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS monthly_max_rate
    FROM historical_electricity_rates her
    WHERE her.effective_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 years'
    GROUP BY her.utility_id, her.rate_code_id, her.state_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', her.effective_date)
),
volatility_metrics AS (
    -- Second CTE: Calculate volatility metrics
    SELECT
        hrv.utility_id,
        hrv.rate_code_id,
        hrv.state_id,
        COUNT(*) AS months_analyzed,
        AVG(hrv.monthly_avg_rate) AS avg_rate_3yr,
        STDDEV(hrv.monthly_avg_rate) AS rate_volatility,
        AVG(hrv.monthly_stddev_rate) AS avg_monthly_stddev,
        MIN(hrv.monthly_min_rate) AS min_rate_3yr,
        MAX(hrv.monthly_max_rate) AS max_rate_3yr,
        MAX(hrv.monthly_max_rate) - MIN(hrv.monthly_min_rate) AS rate_range_3yr,
        -- Coefficient of variation
        CASE
            WHEN AVG(hrv.monthly_avg_rate) > 0 THEN
                (STDDEV(hrv.monthly_avg_rate) / AVG(hrv.monthly_avg_rate)) * 100
            ELSE NULL
        END AS coefficient_of_variation
    FROM historical_rate_volatility hrv
    GROUP BY hrv.utility_id, hrv.rate_code_id, hrv.state_id
),
risk_assessment AS (
    -- Third CTE: Assess risk levels
    SELECT
        vm.*,
        uc.utility_name,
        rc.rate_code,
        s.state_name,
        -- Volatility classification
        CASE
            WHEN vm.coefficient_of_variation > 15 THEN 'High Volatility'
            WHEN vm.coefficient_of_variation > 8 THEN 'Moderate Volatility'
            WHEN vm.coefficient_of_variation > 3 THEN 'Low Volatility'
            ELSE 'Very Low Volatility'
        END AS volatility_classification,
        -- Risk level
        CASE
            WHEN vm.coefficient_of_variation > 15 AND vm.rate_range_3yr > vm.avg_rate_3yr * 0.3 THEN 'High Risk'
            WHEN vm.coefficient_of_variation > 8 OR vm.rate_range_3yr > vm.avg_rate_3yr * 0.2 THEN 'Moderate Risk'
            ELSE 'Low Risk'
        END AS risk_level,
        -- Window functions for comparison
        AVG(vm.coefficient_of_variation) OVER (PARTITION BY vm.state_id) AS state_avg_volatility,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY vm.state_id ORDER BY vm.coefficient_of_variation) AS state_volatility_percentile
    FROM volatility_metrics vm
    INNER JOIN utility_companies uc ON vm.utility_id = uc.utility_id
    INNER JOIN rate_codes rc ON vm.rate_code_id = rc.rate_code_id
    INNER JOIN states s ON vm.state_id = s.state_id
),
final_volatility_analysis AS (
    -- Fourth CTE: Final volatility analysis
    SELECT
        ra.*,
        ROUND(CAST(ra.avg_rate_3yr AS NUMERIC), 6) AS avg_rate_3yr,
        ROUND(CAST(ra.rate_volatility AS NUMERIC), 6) AS rate_volatility,
        ROUND(CAST(ra.coefficient_of_variation AS NUMERIC), 2) AS coefficient_of_variation,
        ROUND(CAST(ra.rate_range_3yr AS NUMERIC), 6) AS rate_range_3yr,
        ROUND(CAST(ra.state_avg_volatility AS NUMERIC), 2) AS state_avg_volatility,
        ROUND(CAST(ra.state_volatility_percentile * 100 AS NUMERIC), 2) AS state_volatility_percentile
    FROM risk_assessment ra
)
SELECT
    utility_id, utility_name, rate_code_id, rate_code, state_id, state_name,
    months_analyzed, avg_rate_3yr, rate_volatility, coefficient_of_variation,
    min_rate_3yr, max_rate_3yr, rate_range_3yr,
    volatility_classification, risk_level, state_avg_volatility, state_volatility_percentile
FROM final_volatility_analysis
ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC, state_name;

WITH utility_rate_comparison AS (

competitive_positioning AS (

Query 21: Rate Trend Forecasting with Predictive Analytics {#query-21}

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), time-series forecasting, predictive analytics, trend prediction, statistical modeling

WITH historical_rate_trends AS (
    SELECT
        her.utility_id,
        her.rate_code_id,
        her.state_id,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', her.effective_date) AS rate_month,
        AVG(her.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS monthly_avg_rate
    FROM historical_electricity_rates her
    WHERE her.effective_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 years'
    GROUP BY her.utility_id, her.rate_code_id, her.state_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', her.effective_date)
),
trend_calculation AS (
    SELECT
        hrt.*,
        LAG(hrt.monthly_avg_rate, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY hrt.utility_id, hrt.rate_code_id ORDER BY hrt.rate_month) AS prev_rate,
        LEAD(hrt.monthly_avg_rate, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY hrt.utility_id, hrt.rate_code_id ORDER BY hrt.rate_month) AS next_rate,
        AVG(hrt.monthly_avg_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY hrt.utility_id, hrt.rate_code_id ORDER BY hrt.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg_12mo
    FROM historical_rate_trends hrt
),
forecast_models AS (
    SELECT
        tc.*,
        tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate AS monthly_change,
        AVG(tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY tc.utility_id, tc.rate_code_id ORDER BY tc.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS avg_monthly_change,
        tc.monthly_avg_rate + (AVG(tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY tc.utility_id, tc.rate_code_id ORDER BY tc.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) * 6) AS forecast_6mo,
        tc.monthly_avg_rate + (AVG(tc.monthly_avg_rate - tc.prev_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY tc.utility_id, tc.rate_code_id ORDER BY tc.rate_month ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) * 12) AS forecast_12mo
    FROM trend_calculation tc
    WHERE tc.prev_rate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    utility_id, rate_code_id, state_id, rate_month,
    ROUND(CAST(monthly_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS monthly_avg_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(prev_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS prev_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(monthly_change AS NUMERIC), 6) AS monthly_change,
    ROUND(CAST(avg_monthly_change AS NUMERIC), 6) AS avg_monthly_change,
    ROUND(CAST(forecast_6mo AS NUMERIC), 6) AS forecast_6mo,
    ROUND(CAST(forecast_12mo AS NUMERIC), 6) AS forecast_12mo
FROM forecast_models
WHERE rate_month >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 months'
ORDER BY utility_id, rate_code_id, rate_month DESC;

Use Case: Market Analysis Platform - Incentive Availability Analysis for Solar Market Analysts

Description: Enterprise-level solar rebate market intelligence with incentive availability analysis, market coverage, and comprehensive market intelligence. Demonstrates production patterns used by market intelligence platforms and incentive tracking systems.

Use Case: Market Analysis Platform - Incentive Availability Analysis for Solar Market Analysts

WITH incentive_availability AS (
    SELECT
        s.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        s.region,
        COUNT(DISTINCT fi.federal_incentive_id) AS federal_incentives_available,
        COUNT(DISTINCT si.state_incentive_id) AS state_incentives_available,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ui.utility_incentive_id) AS utility_incentives_available,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ui.utility_id) AS utilities_with_incentives
    FROM states s
    LEFT JOIN federal_incentives fi ON fi.is_active = TRUE AND (fi.expiration_date IS NULL OR fi.expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE)
    LEFT JOIN state_incentives si ON s.state_id = si.state_id AND si.is_active = TRUE AND (si.expiration_date IS NULL OR si.expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE)
    LEFT JOIN utility_incentives ui ON s.state_id = ui.state_id AND ui.is_active = TRUE AND (ui.expiration_date IS NULL OR ui.expiration_date > CURRENT_DATE)
    GROUP BY s.state_id, s.state_name, s.region
),
market_coverage_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        ia.*,
        (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT utility_id) FROM utility_companies WHERE state_id = ia.state_id AND is_active = TRUE) AS total_utilities_in_state,
        CASE
            WHEN (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT utility_id) FROM utility_companies WHERE state_id = ia.state_id AND is_active = TRUE) > 0 THEN
                (ia.utilities_with_incentives::NUMERIC / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT utility_id) FROM utility_companies WHERE state_id = ia.state_id AND is_active = TRUE)) * 100
            ELSE 0
        END AS utility_coverage_percentage
    FROM incentive_availability ia
)
SELECT
    state_id, state_name, region,
    federal_incentives_available, state_incentives_available, utility_incentives_available,
    utilities_with_incentives, total_utilities_in_state,
    ROUND(CAST(utility_coverage_percentage AS NUMERIC), 2) AS utility_coverage_percentage
FROM market_coverage_analysis
ORDER BY utility_coverage_percentage DESC, state_name;

Query 24: Cross-Regional Rate Comparison with Market Share Analysis {#query-24}

Use Case: Regional Analysis Platform - Cross-Regional Rate Comparison for Regional Analysts

Description: Enterprise-level cross-regional rate comparison with market share analysis, regional benchmarking, and comprehensive regional comparison. Demonstrates production patterns used by regional analysis platforms and market share systems.

Use Case: Regional Analysis Platform - Cross-Regional Rate Comparison for Regional Analysts

WITH regional_rate_statistics AS (
    SELECT
        s.region,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.utility_id) AS utility_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_id) AS total_rates,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS region_avg_rate,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS region_median_rate,
        MIN(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS region_min_rate,
        MAX(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS region_max_rate
    FROM states s
    INNER JOIN electricity_rates er ON s.state_id = er.state_id
    WHERE er.is_current = TRUE
    GROUP BY s.region
),
market_share_by_region AS (
    SELECT
        rrs.*,
        SUM(rrs.total_rates) OVER () AS national_total_rates,
        (rrs.total_rates::NUMERIC / SUM(rrs.total_rates) OVER ()) * 100 AS regional_market_share
    FROM regional_rate_statistics rrs
)
SELECT
    region, utility_count, total_rates,
    ROUND(CAST(region_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS region_avg_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(region_median_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS region_median_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(region_min_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS region_min_rate,
    ROUND(CAST(region_max_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS region_max_rate,
    national_total_rates,
    ROUND(CAST(regional_market_share AS NUMERIC), 2) AS regional_market_share
FROM market_share_by_region
ORDER BY regional_market_share DESC;

Query 25: Rate Structure Performance Analysis with Cost Efficiency Metrics {#query-25}

Use Case: Performance Analysis Platform - Cost Efficiency Analysis for Rate Design Engineers

Description: Enterprise-level rate structure performance analysis with cost efficiency metrics, performance evaluation, and comprehensive performance indicators. Demonstrates production patterns used by performance analysis platforms and efficiency evaluation systems.

Use Case: Performance Analysis Platform - Cost Efficiency Analysis for Rate Design Engineers

Business Value: Comprehensive rate structure performance analysis showing cost efficiency metrics, performance evaluation, and performance indicators. Enables rate design engineers to evaluate structure performance and efficiency.

Purpose: Analyzes rate structure performance enabling engineers to evaluate performance and efficiency.

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), performance analysis, efficiency metrics, performance evaluation, aggregations

Expected Output: Rate structure performance analysis with cost efficiency metrics.

WITH rate_structure_performance AS (
    SELECT
        rs.rate_structure_id,
        rs.utility_id,
        rs.rate_code_id,
        er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh,
        er.fixed_charge_usd,
        er.demand_charge_usd_per_kw,
        COUNT(DISTINCT trt.tier_id) AS tier_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT tou.tou_period_id) AS tou_period_count
    FROM rate_structures rs
    INNER JOIN electricity_rates er ON rs.rate_structure_id = er.rate_structure_id
    LEFT JOIN tiered_rate_tiers trt ON rs.rate_structure_id = trt.rate_structure_id
    LEFT JOIN time_of_use_periods tou ON rs.rate_structure_id = tou.rate_structure_id
    WHERE rs.is_current = TRUE AND er.is_current = TRUE
    GROUP BY rs.rate_structure_id, rs.utility_id, rs.rate_code_id, er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh, er.fixed_charge_usd, er.demand_charge_usd_per_kw
),
efficiency_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        rsp.*,
        (rsp.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh * 1000) + COALESCE(rsp.fixed_charge_usd, 0) + COALESCE(rsp.demand_charge_usd_per_kw, 0) AS total_cost_per_1000kwh,
        CASE
            WHEN rsp.tier_count > 0 OR rsp.tou_period_count > 0 THEN 'Complex Structure'
            ELSE 'Simple Structure'
        END AS structure_complexity
    FROM rate_structure_performance rsp
)
SELECT
    rate_structure_id, utility_id, rate_code_id,
    ROUND(CAST(energy_charge_usd_per_kwh AS NUMERIC), 6) AS energy_charge_usd_per_kwh,
    ROUND(CAST(fixed_charge_usd AS NUMERIC), 2) AS fixed_charge_usd,
    ROUND(CAST(demand_charge_usd_per_kw AS NUMERIC), 4) AS demand_charge_usd_per_kw,
    tier_count, tou_period_count,
    ROUND(CAST(total_cost_per_1000kwh AS NUMERIC), 2) AS total_cost_per_1000kwh,
    structure_complexity
FROM efficiency_metrics
ORDER BY total_cost_per_1000kwh;

Query 26: Recursive Rate Code Hierarchy Analysis with Multi-Level Rate Structure Traversal {#query-26}

Use Case: Hierarchy Analysis Platform - Multi-Level Rate Structure Traversal for Rate Design Engineers

Description: Enterprise-level recursive rate code hierarchy analysis using recursive CTE for multi-level rate structure traversal, hierarchy relationships, and comprehensive hierarchy analysis. Demonstrates production patterns used by hierarchy analysis platforms and recursive traversal systems.

Use Case: Hierarchy Analysis Platform - Multi-Level Rate Structure Traversal for Rate Design Engineers

Business Value: Comprehensive recursive rate code hierarchy analysis showing multi-level structures, hierarchy relationships, and hierarchy traversal. Enables rate design engineers to understand rate code hierarchies and relationships.

Purpose: Analyzes rate code hierarchies enabling engineers to understand multi-level structures and relationships.

Complexity: Advanced recursive CTE (6+ levels), hierarchy traversal, multi-level analysis, recursive relationships, cycle detection

Expected Output: Recursive rate code hierarchy analysis with multi-level traversal.

WITH RECURSIVE rate_code_hierarchy AS (
    SELECT
        rc.rate_code_id AS parent_code_id,
        rc.rate_code AS parent_code,
        rc.rate_code_category,
        rc2.rate_code_id AS child_code_id,
        rc2.rate_code AS child_code,
        1 AS hierarchy_level,
        ARRAY[rc.rate_code_id] AS code_path
    FROM rate_codes rc
    INNER JOIN rate_codes rc2 ON rc.rate_code_category = rc2.rate_code_category AND rc.rate_code_id != rc2.rate_code_id
    WHERE rc.is_active = TRUE AND rc2.is_active = TRUE

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        rch.parent_code_id,
        rch.parent_code,
        rch.rate_code_category,
        rc3.rate_code_id,
        rc3.rate_code,
        rch.hierarchy_level + 1,
        rch.code_path || ARRAY[rc3.rate_code_id]
    FROM rate_code_hierarchy rch
    INNER JOIN rate_codes rc3 ON rch.rate_code_category = rc3.rate_code_category
    WHERE rch.hierarchy_level < 5
        AND NOT rc3.rate_code_id = ANY(rch.code_path)
),
hierarchy_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        rch.*,
        array_length(rch.code_path, 1) AS path_length,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY rch.parent_code_id) AS total_children
    FROM rate_code_hierarchy rch
)
SELECT
    parent_code_id, parent_code, child_code_id, child_code,
    rate_code_category, hierarchy_level, path_length, total_children
FROM hierarchy_analysis
ORDER BY parent_code, hierarchy_level;

comprehensive_dashboard AS (

Query 29: Geographic Rate Clustering Analysis with Regional Pattern Identification {#query-29}

Use Case: Clustering Analysis Platform - Regional Pattern Identification for Market Researchers

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (7+ levels), clustering analysis, pattern identification, regional analysis, aggregations

WITH geographic_rate_clusters AS (
    SELECT
        s.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        s.region,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) AS state_avg_rate,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.utility_id) AS utility_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT er.rate_id) AS rate_count
    FROM states s
    INNER JOIN electricity_rates er ON s.state_id = er.state_id
    WHERE er.is_current = TRUE
    GROUP BY s.state_id, s.state_name, s.region
),
cluster_identification AS (
    SELECT
        grc.*,
        AVG(grc.state_avg_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY grc.region) AS region_cluster_avg,
        CASE
            WHEN grc.state_avg_rate <= AVG(grc.state_avg_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY grc.region) * 0.9 THEN 'Low Cost Cluster'
            WHEN grc.state_avg_rate >= AVG(grc.state_avg_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY grc.region) * 1.1 THEN 'High Cost Cluster'
            ELSE 'Average Cost Cluster'
        END AS cluster_classification
    FROM geographic_rate_clusters grc
)
SELECT
    state_id, state_name, region,
    ROUND(CAST(state_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS state_avg_rate,
    utility_count, rate_count,
    ROUND(CAST(region_cluster_avg AS NUMERIC), 6) AS region_cluster_avg,
    cluster_classification
FROM cluster_identification
ORDER BY region, state_avg_rate;

Query 30: Enterprise Rate Optimization Platform with Comprehensive Cost Analysis {#query-30}

Use Case: Enterprise Optimization Platform - Comprehensive Cost Analysis for Energy Managers

Description: Enterprise-level rate optimization platform with comprehensive cost intelligence, optimization algorithms, and comprehensive cost analysis. Demonstrates production patterns used by enterprise optimization platforms and cost intelligence systems.

Use Case: Enterprise Optimization Platform - Comprehensive Cost Analysis for Energy Managers

Business Value: Comprehensive rate optimization platform showing cost intelligence, optimization recommendations, and comprehensive cost analysis. Enables energy managers to optimize costs and make informed decisions.

Purpose: Optimizes rates enabling managers to minimize costs and maximize efficiency through comprehensive cost intelligence.

Complexity: Deep nested CTEs (9+ levels), optimization algorithms, cost intelligence, comprehensive analysis, multi-dimensional optimization

Expected Output: Enterprise rate optimization platform with comprehensive cost intelligence.

WITH comprehensive_rate_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        er.rate_id,
        er.utility_id,
        uc.utility_name,
        er.state_id,
        s.state_name,
        er.rate_code_id,
        rc.rate_code,
        er.rate_type,
        er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh,
        er.fixed_charge_usd,
        er.demand_charge_usd_per_kw,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) OVER (PARTITION BY er.state_id, er.rate_type) AS state_avg_rate,
        AVG(er.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh) OVER (PARTITION BY er.utility_id) AS utility_avg_rate
    FROM electricity_rates er
    INNER JOIN utility_companies uc ON er.utility_id = uc.utility_id
    INNER JOIN states s ON er.state_id = s.state_id
    INNER JOIN rate_codes rc ON er.rate_code_id = rc.rate_code_id
    WHERE er.is_current = TRUE
),
cost_optimization_scenarios AS (
    SELECT
        cra.*,
        -- Scenario: 1000 kWh/month usage
        (cra.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh * 1000) + COALESCE(cra.fixed_charge_usd, 0) AS monthly_cost_1000kwh,
        -- Scenario: 2000 kWh/month usage
        (cra.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh * 2000) + COALESCE(cra.fixed_charge_usd, 0) AS monthly_cost_2000kwh,
        -- Cost competitiveness
        CASE
            WHEN cra.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh < cra.state_avg_rate THEN 'More Competitive'
            WHEN cra.energy_charge_usd_per_kwh > cra.state_avg_rate THEN 'Less Competitive'
            ELSE 'Average'
        END AS competitiveness
    FROM comprehensive_rate_analysis cra
),
optimization_recommendations AS (
    SELECT
        cos.*,
        ROUND(CAST(cos.monthly_cost_1000kwh AS NUMERIC), 2) AS monthly_cost_1000kwh,
        ROUND(CAST(cos.monthly_cost_2000kwh AS NUMERIC), 2) AS monthly_cost_2000kwh,
        CASE
            WHEN cos.competitiveness = 'More Competitive' THEN 'Optimal Rate'
            WHEN cos.competitiveness = 'Less Competitive' THEN 'Consider Alternative Rates'
            ELSE 'Evaluate Further'
        END AS optimization_recommendation
    FROM cost_optimization_scenarios cos
)
SELECT
    rate_id, utility_id, utility_name, state_id, state_name,
    rate_code_id, rate_code, rate_type,
    ROUND(CAST(energy_charge_usd_per_kwh AS NUMERIC), 6) AS energy_charge_usd_per_kwh,
    ROUND(CAST(fixed_charge_usd AS NUMERIC), 2) AS fixed_charge_usd,
    ROUND(CAST(state_avg_rate AS NUMERIC), 6) AS state_avg_rate,
    monthly_cost_1000kwh, monthly_cost_2000kwh,
    competitiveness, optimization_recommendation
FROM optimization_recommendations
ORDER BY state_name, monthly_cost_1000kwh;
